articles.description: Brazil's state-controlled oil producer Petrobras posted lower-than-expected earnings.

articles.title: Saudis Tell OPEC Production Surged to Highest Since War Began
articles.description: Saudi Arabia told OPEC that its crude oil production climbed by 26 percent last month to the highest since before the outbreak of the war.

articles.title: Amplitude reports upside at Annie-2 well offshore Australia
articles.description: Amplitude Energy has completed and cased its Annie-2 development well offshore Victoria, Australia, reporting preliminary data that indicates improved reservoir characteristics compared with the original Annie discovery.

articles.title: USA Gasoline Falls Below $4 for 1st Time Since August
articles.description: U.S. gasoline fell below $4 per gallon for the first time since August, but the midterm elections weren't the cause, a new GasBuddy blog outlined.

articles.title: Public Support for UK Oil, Gas Higher than Ever, OEUK Says
articles.description: Public support for UK oil and gas production is higher than ever, industry body Offshore Energies UK (OEUK) said.

articles.title: Russia and Ukraine Resume Push for Peace Deal
articles.description: Ukraine and Russia started a second day of U.S.-led peace talks in Abu Dhabi.

articles.title: ExxonMobil CEO to Miss UN Climate Talks
articles.description: The chief executive of ExxonMobil Holdings Corp. is ending his streak of attending United Nations climate conferences.

articles.title: Saudi Crude Output Jumps 26% as Riyadh Reports Near Pre-War Production
articles.description: Saudi Arabia told OPEC it raised crude production in October to 10.563 million barrels per day, back near pre-war levels and slightly above its OPEC quota of about 10.5 million bpd, Bloomberg columnist Javier Blas reported on Wednesday. Output rose 26% from 8.372 million bpd in September to the highest level since February, when the kingdom reported 10.882 million bpd in the last month before the Iran war disrupted Middle East supply, according to Reuters. Riyadh’s official data put supply to the market, net of storage, at 9.203 million bpd,…

articles.title: Orlen terminates QatarEnergy LNG deal after force majeure
articles.description: Orlen has terminated one of its two long-term liquefied natural gas (LNG) supply contracts with QatarEnergy, following an ongoing force majeure event that prevented the supplier from fulfilling its delivery obligations.

articles.title: US DOE approves $480m loan for Arena Energy’s Project Elkhorn
articles.description: The US Department of Energy (DOE) has finalised a $480m loan for Arena Energy’s wholly owned subsidiary Elkhorn Offshore for Project Elkhorn, an offshore oil and gas project off Louisiana in the Gulf of Mexico.

articles.title: Iran War Breathes New Life Into Turkmenistan’s $10 Billion Pipeline Dream
articles.description: At an energy forum in Ashgabat in late October, Turkmenistan made an unexpected announcement. After years of delays and speculation that the project would be canceled, the forum audience was told the Turkmenistan-Afghanistan-Pakistan-India (TAPI) gas pipeline had just reached "the outskirts of Herat" and would be "commissioned by the end of 2026." Depending on one's definition of "outskirts" for the northwestern Afghan city, that first claim appears to be true. Satellite images made on November 7 show the natural gas pipeline extending from Turkmenistan's…

articles.title: India Approves $7.3 Billion High-Capacity Power Link to Back Renewables
articles.description: India has just approved plans for a high-capacity power transmission corridor to help bring electricity from generation to demand centers. The 1,150-kilovolt (kV) system, which will be India’s highest-voltage power corridor, is expected to cost about $7.34 billion (688 billion Indian rupees). At present, most of India’s transmission network consists of 765-kV lines. The plan, approved by the national transmission panel this week, is estimated to take about six years to build. The first phase of the power corridor project includes…

articles.title: Ukrainian Drone Attack Sparks Fire at Russia’s Key Baltic Oil Export Hub
articles.description: A Ukrainian drone attack hit the key Russian commodity export hub Ust-Luga on the Baltic Sea early on Wednesday, as Russia and Ukraine continue to trade strikes on each other’s energy infrastructure amid ongoing U.S.-mediated talks in Abu Dhabi. Drones hit the port area of Ust-Luga, Alexander Drozdenko, the governor of the Leningrad region, said in a Telegram post on Wednesday. A preliminary investigation indicates that the drone attack struck the port area of Ust-Luga, sparking a fire. Efforts to extinguish the fire are…

articles.title: Diamondback, KKR to buy Five Point’s 70% stake in Deep Blue
articles.description: Diamondback Energy and KKR have agreed to acquire Five Point Infrastructure’s 70% stake in Midland Basin water operator Deep Blue Midland Basin for cash.

articles.title: India Eyes 50% Wind Power Capacity Boost Without Acquiring More Land
articles.description: India’s wind turbine manufacturers are in discussions with state and federal authorities about a plan to repower old turbines with higher-capacity, higher-efficiency new ones to boost power output without sacrificing more land. Modern turbines can replace a total of 8 gigawatts (GW) of old and less efficient turbines, Aditya Pyasi, CEO of the Indian Wind Turbine Manufacturers Association, told Bloomberg in an interview published on Wednesday. The repowering project could boost capacity at these sites by nearly 50%, according to estimates…

articles.title: RWE and KKR Seal $16 Billion UK Offshore Wind Mega-Deal
articles.description: German energy company RWE and global investment firm KKR will invest $16 billion (£12 billion) in offshore wind projects in the UK in what is likely the biggest renewable energy investment in Britain ever. RWE and KKR expect to deliver the Vanguard West and Vanguard East offshore wind projects in the UK North Sea with this investment after reaching financial close for both projects. Together, the projects, representing £12 billion investment including the construction of the wind farms and their associated transmission infrastructure,…

articles.title: Siemens Energy More Than Triples Dividend After Record Year
articles.description: Siemens Energy proposes to more than triple its dividend for the fiscal year 2026 ended on September 30 after booking record revenues and orders, driven by the grid and gas turbine businesses amid soaring electricity demand. The Germany-based Siemens Energy on Wednesday said it delivered a record fiscal year 2026, meeting or exceeding all targets that it had raised earlier this year. Siemens Energy’s revenue grew by 15.5% on a comparable basis to $49.3 billion (44.2 billion euros), with capacity expansions at existing Gas Services and Grid…

articles.title: Saudi Arabia and Turkey Sign Major 3 GW Wind Power Deal
articles.description: Saudi Arabia and Turkey have signed an agreement to advance 3 GW of wind power projects in Turkey as part of a broader 5 GW renewable energy program agreed earlier this year. The program, led by Saudi Arabia’s ACWA Power, comprises 2 GW of solar projects in Sivas and Karaman in the first phase and 3 GW of wind projects in the second, Reuters reported, citing the Turkish energy ministry. The latest agreement advances the planned wind phase rather than expanding an existing wind installation. The installed wind capacity to be built under the…

articles.title: Poland's Orlen Becomes First Buyer to Cancel Long-Term Qatar LNG Deal
articles.description: Polish state-owned energy firm Orlen has become the first long-term client of QatarEnergy to cancel an LNG supply contract with the Qatari company amid the continued force majeure on exports. In a regulatory filing from late Tuesday, the Polish firm noted that QatarEnergy has become unable to meet its contractual obligations to supply Orlen with 1 million tons of superchilled gas annually. The contract was signed in 2009, The National noted in a report on the news, and deliveries began in 2016, with the term of the contract until 2034. At the end…

articles.title: Oil Prices Rise as Iran Peace Optimism Fades
articles.description: Crude oil prices reversed their fall from earlier this week as traders grew less optimistic about a peace deal between the United States and Iran amid continuing tanker attacks in the Strait of Hormuz, with a record number of such attacks in October. At the time of writing, Brent crude was trading at $92.43 per barrel, with West Texas Intermediate at $86.62 per barrel, both up from the start of the week but still sharply down from the end of October, when Brent crude was over $110 per barrel, and WTI was over $100. articles.title: Oil Prices Retreat as Peace Hopes Grow
articles.description: Crude extended its decline as diplomatic hopes and recovering Persian Gulf oil flows weighed on prices.

articles.title: Middle East Oil Flows Far from Normal Despite Signs of Oversupply
articles.description: Crude oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz and the whole Middle Eastern region have recovered to close to pre-war levels, vessel-tracking services have been signaling for over a month now. Middle Eastern benchmarks have been weakening for weeks, suggesting an oil glut may be building amid rebounding Persian Gulf exports and global demand destruction amid high prices. On the face of it, an oversupply of crude oil could be forming. But the costs to refiners and consumers are not falling. War, insurance premiums, and record tanker rates have raised…

articles.title: South Sudan Courts Oil Investors as Sudan’s Warring Forces Take Their Share
articles.description: South Sudan is courting fresh capital for 14 exploration blocks and a production increase from roughly 170,000 barrels per day to 230,000, which investors would find impossible to control once those barrels left the country. Captive to neighboring Sudan’s civil war, South Sudan is essentially divvying up its oil, under duress, between the Sudanese Army and the rival paramilitary RSF, which extract payment before the oil can reach the Red Sea. The government-backed South Sudan Oil & Power conference will put that proposition before investors…
